g0-measure.title: Settle the #600 open question by measurement
g0-measure.imperative: REASONING GATE -- no crew. Crew waiver reason: the deliverable is a diagnosis, not code or an independently-verifiable change, and the Commander already holds the whole context the diagnosis turns on; a crew here would be shallower, not safer (commander-core.md, 'Crew gate vs reasoning gate'). Settle which mechanism leaves a reading the acting agent does not own in place at the instant of a trip. Two candidates were offered by the launch order: (1) the write is skipped on an ambiguous or unresolvable binding and the stale file survives; (2) another agent's key resolves into the same directory and writes its own fill. Drive the REAL handle_post_tool_use in a fresh process against a real binding store, real transcript files, and the real payload shapes the harness sends -- never a patched _read_gauge and never a hand-injected CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. Capture gauge.json and .agent-work/.spine-rail-binding.json as artifacts. A measured negative is a complete deliverable (launch order, Honest-Null Clause): if neither candidate is reproduced, report that and stop rather than designing against the wrong mechanism.

g1-implement.title: #600: a gauge reading is named for the agent that produced it
g1-implement.imperative: ONE gate, not three, deliberately: the writer, the reader and the engine must change together or the suite is red between gates, and a planned red window bridged by waivers is a plan smell (commander-core.md). Implement decision:owner-in-the-filename and decision:no-shared-file-fallback per .agent-work/cleanup-b-context-identity/PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md candidate B. The writer (scripts/hooks/gauge_writer_hook.py) already resolves a binding entry that carries engine_session; write the record to gauge-<owner>.json beside the spine instead of gauge.json, and let the two existing sidecars follow that name (they are derived with .with_name() off the gauge path). The engine (scripts/checklist_engine.py, _gauge_path and the trip region only) knows its own active lease session_id; resolve the gauge path from it. When no owner is resolvable on either side, write nothing and read nothing -- decision:unattributable-means-no-reading, fail OPEN, no new refusal. Do NOT fall back to a shared gauge.json: that reinstates the folder-owned file this issue exists to remove. Reuse spine_rail.is_usable_agent_id's allowlist idiom for filename safety rather than inventing a second identity predicate; you may READ spine_rail.py but it is FENCED for edits (lane C). FIRST TASK, before any edit: enumerate BY COMMAND -- never by memory -- every artifact that asserts the literal name gauge.json (code, tests, docs, templates, skills) and STATE THE COUNT in the result; that enumeration is the blast radius of this change and the author is the only one positioned to know it. Evidence standard, inherited from tests/test_checklist_engine.py::TripGaugeReadingOwnership: red-before / green-after over BEHAVIOR, driving the real reader and a real gauge file, never a patched _read_gauge. Hook code cannot be validated from inside the session that contains it -- validate in a fresh process, never a fixture that hand-injects CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.

g1-review.imperative: Independently verify the g1 diff against the close criteria. Specifically check, and do not take the implementer's word for any of them: (a) the governor never REFUSES anywhere it previously permitted -- enumerate the refusal paths rather than sampling them; (b) there is no fallback to a shared gauge.json anywhere on the read or write side; (c) the enumeration of artifacts asserting the literal name gauge.json is complete and its COUNT is stated -- re-run the enumeration yourself, because an under-inclusive sweep reports clean precisely because it never reached the interesting items; (d) the red-before/green-after evidence drives the real reader and a real gauge file, not a patched _read_gauge; (e) no fenced file was edited. Reproduce every pasted command yourself.
